text: A hacker breaks into a website and steals every single password. And they're completely useless to him.
How is that even possible? Stay with me, because the answer is hiding in a kitchen blender.
First, a secret. Good websites never keep your password. Not even the company can see it.
Instead, they drop it into a one way blender. Sunflower seven goes in, and out comes a smoothie of random letters.
And here's the magic. You can turn fruit into a smoothie, but you can never turn a smoothie back into fruit.
Change just one letter, and the smoothie comes out completely different.
So when you log in, the site blends what you typed, and checks if the two smoothies match. Match? You're in.
But hackers are clever. They blend millions of common passwords and look for a match. Password one two three? Cracked instantly.
So sites add a pinch of salt. A random sprinkle for every person, so the same password makes a different smoothie.
And they blend it slowly, thousands of times over. One guess is nothing, but billions of guesses take forever.
That's why the stolen list was useless. Just salty, slow smoothies.
Orbi Transfer takes it further. Your code never even leaves your phone. It's blended three hundred and ten thousand times into the key that locks your file.
The server only keeps a smoothie of a smoothie. Twelve wrong guesses, and the file locks itself. Thirty minutes later, it's gone.
Orbi Transfer dot com. Now you know where your password really goes.
